paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithm for Local-Volatility Option Pricing via the Kolmogorov Equation

summary: This paper presents a theoretical gate-based quantum algorithm for European vanilla option pricing under a local-volatility model by solving the forward Kolmogorov PDE via Schrödingerisation, clock-dimension embedding, and swap-test payoff recovery. The paper reports asymptotic single-asset scaling of O(N^2 log N log log N) versus classical O(N^3), with multi-asset one-step evolution scaling as O(d^5), but it does not include any hardware experiment or empirical benchmark.

experiments.description: End-to-end gate-based quantum algorithm for pricing European vanilla options under a local-volatility model by solving the Kolmogorov forward PDE via Schrödingerisation, time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation with a clock register, and swap-test-based payoff recovery.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based Hamiltonian simulation for the forward Kolmogorov equation with clock-dimension embedding

hyperparameters.volatility_parameterization: polynomial in space and time, sigma(s,t)=sum_{k=0..D_s,q=0..D_t} C_kq s^k t^q
hyperparameters.sparsity_assumption: s=5 in the main complexity table; s=3 in the block-encoding theorem statement

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state prepared as computational basis state |S0> (or sharply peaked Gaussian alternative); auxiliary states prepared as smooth cut-off / polynomial approximations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option-price distribution p(x,t) encoded in amplitudes of an n-qubit main register; auxiliary w-register for Schrödingerisation and y-register for clock dimension; initial delta distribution encoded as |S0> or Gaussian approximation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute discounted option price V0 = e^{-∫_0^T r(s)ds} E[C0(S_T)] by solving the forward Kolmogorov PDE and evaluating the payoff expectation via swap test
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on positive momentum eigenvectors; no explicit penalty formulation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Time-dependent pseudo-Hamiltonian H_LV embedded into unitary Hamiltonian H = I⊗I_w⊗p_y + H_LVS(t=x_y)
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: n_w + n_y + (ancillas for state preparation and swap test, not fully enumerated)

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call/put option pricing under a local-volatility model; includes single-asset and multi-asset forward Kolmogorov PDE formulations

dataset_specification.description: No market dataset specified; model-based pricing with Black-Scholes and local-volatility examples

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Volatility surface modeled as polynomial approximation; discretization over asset-price domain [a,b] with grid size Δx=(b-a)/(2^n-1)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical resource analysis; swap-test overlap estimation; scalability discussion for single-asset and d-asset cases

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical input consists of current spot price S0 and fitted local-volatility surface coefficients; payoff discretization and polynomial approximation used for state preparation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Swap-test probabilities converted to overlaps; overlaps combined with analytic normalization factors to recover call/put prices

classical_baselines.value: first order in time; g-th order in space

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup; simplified single-asset scaling O(N^2 log N log log N) vs O(N^3)
speedup_claims.conditions: single-asset discussion; assuming block-encoding-based Hamiltonian simulation and the paper's simplified scaling regime
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as an asymptotic/resource-analysis result, not an experimental benchmark. The speedup is polynomial, not exponential, for the single-asset case.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential speedup in dimension / mitigation of curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.conditions: high-dimensional basket or multi-asset pricing; forward Kolmogorov formulation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper argues the quantum framework admits exponential scaling advantage with respect to dimension, but the detailed theorem given states one-step evolution cost scales polynomially in d (O(d^5)); the claim is about avoiding classical exponential blowup in dimension.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic improvement in grid size for the single dimension discretization
speedup_claims.conditions: single-asset discretization with N = 2^n grid points
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper describes this as a polynomial advantage in grid size; the exact simplified comparison is O(N^2 polylog N) vs O(N^3).

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Initial-state preparation O(n log n) for piecewise-polynomial states; Hamiltonian simulation via block-encoding and QSP-based methods scales as O(N^2 log N log log N) in the paper’s simplified single-asset discussion; multi-asset evolution cost scales polynomially in d, stated as O(d^5) for one time-evolution step
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical finite-difference / exponential-integration methods scale as O(s T N^3) in the paper’s simplified analysis

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; the paper gives asymptotic scaling only, with single-asset quantum cost simplified to O(N^2 log N log log N) versus classical O(N^3), and multi-asset one-step cost O(d^5).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large grid sizes N=2^n and high-dimensional basket pricing; the paper argues the main benefit is avoiding classical curse-of-dimensionality, but no concrete crossover point is computed.
limiting_factors: Hamiltonian norm scales as ~2^(2n), limiting practical advantage
State preparation and swap-test readout overheads
Need for block-encoding/oracle constructions and auxiliary registers
Quadratic single-asset speedup is unlikely to survive fault-tolerance overheads

notes: No actual hardware experiment is reported; the paper is a theoretical algorithm/resource-analysis preprint.
The paper provides asymptotic gate/query complexity and some explicit CNOT counts for state preparation, but not a full compiled circuit depth or shot count.
num_qubits inferred from the described registers n, n_w, and n_y; the paper explicitly states the register structure but not a single instantiated numeric qubit count.

The paper claims asymptotic polynomial advantage for single-asset discretization and exponential-in-dimension scaling for multi-asset problems, but provides no experimental benchmark or crossover analysis.
Per Hoefler et al., this remains theoretical because the paper does not demonstrate practical advantage on hardware or noisy simulation.
